seo.metaTitle: Gamma Correction PNG - Free Brightness Fix, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Lift or drop the midtones without touching black or white. Free, no upload, no signup - gamma correction runs on your device, in your browser, instantly.
seo.longDescription: Gamma correction reshapes the midtones of a picture without moving the black and white end points. The value is used as a lookup on every channel: below 1 the curve pulls midtones down so the picture darkens, above 1 it lifts them so it brightens, and exactly 1 leaves the image alone. That is the tool for a washed-out scan, a photo that looks flat next to a screenshot, or an image saved with the wrong gamma assumption. It runs in your browser and keeps the alpha channel intact.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Below 1 darkens the midtones, above 1 lifts them, 1 is the untouched original.
Black and white end points stay put — unlike the brightness slider, nothing clips.
The alpha channel and the dimensions never change.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Gamma below 1 for darker midtones or above 1 for lighter ones; 1 is the untouched original.
Work in small steps - the slider moves by 0.05, and past about 1.6 the shadows start to block up.
Download the result from the Download button.

faq.q: Is this the same as the brightness slider?
faq.a: They overlap but are not equal. Brightness shifts every value by the same amount and clips at the ends, while gamma bends the curve: the ends of the range stay put and only the middle moves, so gamma lifts the shadows without flattening the highlights.

faq.q: Where does the value 1 come from?
faq.a: It is the identity - the assumption that the stored values are already right. A value below 1 says the image was encoded too dark for the display and needs lifting; above 1 says it was encoded too light.

faq.q: Does it change resolution or alpha?
faq.a: Neither. The same pixels come out at the same size, the alpha channel is copied through unchanged, and only the red, green and blue lookup changes.

faq.q: My whole picture is too dark and gamma is not enough. What next?
faq.a: Try the auto contrast tool, which measures the actual darkest and brightest values in your image and stretches them to the full range instead of applying a fixed curve. If only the color cast is wrong, the temperature tool shifts red and blue.
